issues.description: DIRECT_MONOTONIC_BLOCK_SHIFT constant duplicated/relocated may break binary read compatibility
issues.detail: The static import in Lucene99ScalarQuantizedVectorsWriter changed from Lucene99FlatVectorsFormat.DIRECT_MONOTONIC_BLOCK_SHIFT to the new local constant in Lucene99ScalarQuantizedVectorsFormat. If the values differ (or were intentionally shared), this silently changes on-disk layout encoding. Verify both equal 16 and confirm no read path still references the original location for legacy segments.

issues.description: SPI NAME constant downgraded from public to package-private may break service loader / named lookup
issues.detail: Lucene99HnswScalarQuantizedVectorsFormat.NAME and Lucene99ScalarQuantizedVectorsFormat.NAME were changed from public to package-private. External tooling and any NamedSPILoader.lookup(NAME) callers (including back-compat tests loading by name string) will fail to resolve. Verify no public API or codec registration relies on the public NAME constant.

issues.description: Reader path may still need the writer-only constants now scoped package-private in a different module
issues.detail: Lucene99ScalarQuantizedVectorsWriter is now under backward-codecs/test, but it references package-private constants from Lucene99ScalarQuantizedVectorsFormat (DIRECT_MONOTONIC_BLOCK_SHIFT, QUANTIZED_VECTOR_COMPONENT, calculateDefaultConfidenceInterval). This compiles since both are in the same package, but production read paths in core that previously imported these via public access will break. Confirm core no longer needs them.

issues.description: Lucene99HnswVectorsReader still referenced from backward-codecs package but lives in core
issues.detail: The moved Lucene99HnswScalarQuantizedVectorsFormat now imports org.apache.lucene.codecs.lucene99.Lucene99HnswVectorsReader/Format from core. This creates a backward->core dependency which is typically forbidden in Lucene's module layering. Verify backward-codecs module-info permits this and that Lucene99HnswVectorsFormat itself isn't slated for deprecation, which would cascade.

issues.description: Removed @Deprecated annotation contradicts the stated goal of preventing user writes
issues.detail: Both Lucene99ScalarQuantizedVectorsFormat and Lucene99HnswScalarQuantizedVectorsFormat had @Deprecated removed during the move. Since the format is now read-only (fieldsWriter throws UnsupportedOperationException), the deprecation is more important than ever to warn users at compile time. Without it, users have no signal until runtime failure.

issues.description: Lucene99HnswScalarQuantizedVectorsFormat constructor still validates numMergeWorkers/mergeExec but discards them
issues.detail: The constructor keeps the validation throwing on numMergeWorkers > 1 with null executor (and vice versa), but no longer stores numMergeWorkers or mergeExec. This is dead validation for a write path that now throws UnsupportedOperationException unconditionally. Consider simplifying the constructor or documenting why validation is kept (back-compat of public API surface).

review.summary: This PR moves the legacy Lucene99 scalar-quantized vector formats from core to backward-codecs and makes them read-only by throwing UnsupportedOperationException in fieldsWriter. The mechanical rename is mostly clean, but several concerns stand out: removal of @Deprecated annotations weakens the user-facing signal that these formats are legacy; the NAME constants were downgraded from public to package-private which may break SPI/named lookups; a constant (DIRECT_MONOTONIC_BLOCK_SHIFT) was effectively relocated and needs verification it matches the original 16 used on disk; and the moved class still has back-references into core (Lucene99HnswVectorsReader/Format), which may violate Lucene's module layering. The test split into V0 and V1 writers is reasonable for covering both legacy on-disk versions.
